# popmex <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-universe](https://fdzul.r-universe.dev/badges/popmex)](https://fdzul.r-universe.dev/popmex)
<!-- badges: end -->

popmex provides population datasets of Mexico for epidemiological analysis
and to calculate rates, at municipal and hexagon (400 m) resolution. It is
part of the [dengueverse](https://fdzul.r-universe.dev).

## Datasets

**Population in 400 m H3 hexagons** (Kontur, [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/kontur-population-mexico)):

- `hdx_pop2023`, `hdx_pop2022` and `hdx_pop2021`. Estimated inhabitants per hexagon.

**Population by municipality**:

- `pop2020`, `pop2010` and `pop2000`. Census population by sex and age group from the
  territorial indicators (ITER) of the Population and Housing Censuses of
  [INEGI](https://www.inegi.org.mx/app/scitel/Default?ev=9).
- `conapop`. Reconstruction (1990-2020) and projections (2021-2040) of the population
  of the 2,475 municipalities by sex and age group, from
  [CONAPO](https://www.gob.mx/conapo/documentos/reconstruccion-y-proyecciones-de-la-poblacion-de-los-municipios-de-mexico-1990-2040).

## Installation

``` r
install.packages("popmex",
                 repos = c("https://fdzul.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

## Example

``` r
library(popmex)

# hexagons of the metropolitan area of Mérida, 2023
merida <- extract_pop(year = 2023, cve_edo = "31",
                      locality = c("Merida", "Uman", "Kanasin"))
sum(merida$population)

# population of each municipality in 2020, to use as denominator
head(pop2020[, c("CVEGEO", "pobtot", "pobfem", "pobmas")])
```

## Credits

The hexagon datasets come from the Kontur Population dataset published in the
Humanitarian Data Exchange ([HDX](https://data.humdata.org)). The municipal
datasets come from INEGI and CONAPO.

## Inspiration

The spatial dataset provided by the package were inspired by the need to contribute to decision making in programs
of Vector Transmitted Diseases (VTE) and Arthropod Venom Intoxication (IVA) of the CENAPRECE of the Secretary of Health of Mexico
